rst31-integration-q001.explanation: The general diagram places pectoral fins behind gill covers, pelvic fins at the front underside and anal fins at the rear underside. Do not ignore species variation and assert this for every fish.

rst31-integration-q002.objective: Combine general hygiene and important-process controls in plans and communicate implementation.
rst31-integration-q002.stem: The manager plans only critical heating, leaving cleaning/handwashing to individuals. Which improvement fits?
options: Only managers read plans; staff see only results
Heating records make cleaning/handwashing plans and communication unnecessary
Include general hygiene and check staff can explain work/abnormality reporting
Plan only cleaning and leave heating to experience
reasons: Communication to implementing staff is missing.
Important-process controls do not remove general hygiene.
This combines controls and checks understanding/implementation.
General hygiene cannot replace important-process controls.
rst31-integration-q002.explanation: HACCP-based management combines both and communicates plans for implementation; documents alone are insufficient.

rst31-integration-q003.objective: Distinguish voluntary-recall decisions from notification checks.
rst31-integration-q003.stem: A relevant food recall begins. Someone says voluntary recalls need no notification. Which judgement fits?
options: All voluntary recalls need none, regardless of food/reason
Separate recall and notification decisions; check scope/conditions with managers/health authorities
Keep serving suspect food normally until notification checks finish
Treat every return identically and omit food/reason records
reasons: The name voluntary alone cannot establish exemption.
This separates decisions/notification and checks individual conditions.
Prevent health harm during checks; this does not justify normal service.
Food/reason records support checks/communication; not every return is identical.
rst31-integration-q003.explanation: Starting a voluntary recall and checking statutory notification are separate. Check scope/exceptions and record food, reasons and action; do not assume voluntary means exempt.

rst31-integration-q004.objective: Distinguish food-hygiene supervisor duties from operator direction/responsibility.
rst31-integration-q004.stem: An operator appoints a food-hygiene supervisor. Which role fits?
options: The supervisor manages hygiene under operator direction and shares issues
Appointment removes the operator from hygiene management
Operator instructions mean the supervisor need not perform hygiene work
The supervisor withholds known hygiene problems
reasons: This combines supervisor practice and operator role.
Appointment does not free the operator from involvement.
Receiving directions does not remove implementation duties.
Unshared problems do not lead to necessary improvements.
rst31-integration-q004.explanation: The supervisor follows operator direction. Appointment does not eliminate operator responsibility; share hygiene opinions/issues.

rst31-integration-q005.objective: Check everyday infection prevention and self-protection during vomit/faeces cleanup.
rst31-integration-q005.stem: A cook cleans family vomit at home. Which matches prevention principles?
options: Gloves eliminate infection risk, so other measures need no check
Home infection is unrelated to work; bare hands are fine
Take care at home too, using disposable mask/gloves/apron for protection
Wear dirty work clothes to prevent home infection
reasons: Gloves alone do not eliminate infection possibility.
Home infection can make food handlers contamination sources.
This combines home prevention with specified self-protection.
Dirty workwear is not prevention and may spread contamination.
rst31-integration-q005.explanation: Food handlers guard against infection in everyday/home life. Disposable mask/gloves/apron protect during faeces/vomit cleanup; detailed methods/chemicals require separate checking.

rst31-integration-q007.objective: Connect hospitality with concrete considerate actions and repeated practice.
rst31-integration-q007.stem: A newcomer says hospitality needs feeling but no movement practice. Which advice fits?
options: Repeatedly practise clean, kind, courteous actions expressing care
Identical actions for everyone remove the need to ask wishes
Good intentions remove cleanliness/courtesy checks
Continue unwanted help to look kind
reasons: This connects intention/action and basic-skill learning.
Basic actions still require checking wishes.
Intentions do not justify omitting cleanliness/courtesy.
Ignoring preferences is not caring for someone.
rst31-integration-q007.explanation: Express consideration in concrete actions, learning/practising basics and checking circumstances/wishes. This is not attributing one trait to nationalities/groups.

rst31-integration-q008.objective: Understand accumulated small dissatisfactions and enquire early.
rst31-integration-q008.stem: Repeated short waits and insufficient explanations precede a strong complaint. Which response fits?
options: Only the last incident must matter; ignore earlier events
Consider accumulated small dissatisfactions and ask carefully what was wrong
Short individual waits cannot accumulate dissatisfaction
Judge personality alone without checking explanations/service
reasons: Earlier circumstances may matter, not just the final incident.
Treat accumulation as a possibility and verify through the guest’s account.
Short waits combined with poor explanations can increase dissatisfaction.
Personality assumptions alone miss service problems.
rst31-integration-q008.explanation: Several small dissatisfactions can precede a complaint. Do not assume one cause; listen and establish circumstances.

rst31-operations2-role-judgment.title: Cross-check roles and reporting on one sheet
rst31-operations2-role-judgment.text: The shift supervisor maintains QSC during the shift and also coordinates ordering, receiving and storage checks, utility costs, customer relations, working hours, new-staff training and cover for absences. Link each task, decision authority and reporting route to the manager in a role chart. For example, when short-staffed, adjust stations within your authority and request cover; changes to opening hours or expenditure follow the store’s approval process. Learn who can do what, rather than merely memorising job titles.

rst31-operations2-monthly-cost-log.title: A log entry linking a difference to its cause and follow-up
rst31-operations2-monthly-cost-log.text: An independent monthly exercise uses sales of 1,000,000 yen, standard cost of 300,000 yen, opening inventory of 100,000 yen, purchases of 330,000 yen and closing inventory of 110,000 yen. Actual cost is 320,000 yen. Defining loss as “actual − standard” gives a loss of 20,000 yen and a rate difference of 32% − 30% = +2 percentage points. One log entry might read “+2 points / suspected overportioning / observe weighing / person responsible A / recheck next week”; do not declare a cause before confirming it. Also inspect inventory, receiving and waste records, then compare results after improvement using the same formula. Implement the monthly countermeasures in daily work and have the responsible person record the checks.

rst31-operations2-interview-check.title: Check application documents only as needed for the job
rst31-operations2-interview-check.text: During the interview, confirm the applicant’s stated experience, qualifications and availability, and use the photograph or other appropriate information to avoid confusing applicants. Where age verification is needed for the job, such as restrictions on young workers, check its purpose and method with recruitment or HR and handle it appropriately. Do not base hiring solely on age or request family or registered-domicile information unrelated to aptitude and ability. The document example in the textbook does not justify demanding unnecessary additional identity records from every applicant.

rst31-operations2-service-phrases.title: Match eight basic service expressions to situations
rst31-operations2-service-phrases.text: Distinguish “いらっしゃいませ” (Welcome) on arrival, “かしこまりました” (Certainly) when accepting a request, “少々お待ちください” (Please wait a moment) before a short wait, and “お待たせいたしました” (Thank you for waiting) when returning afterwards. “失礼いたします” (Excuse me) is a basic expression when moving near a guest to carry out a task; “恐れ入りますが” (Sorry to trouble you, but…) introduces a request; “申し訳ございません” (I am very sorry) apologises for a mistake; and “ありがとうございました” (Thank you very much) expresses appreciation for the visit. Volume, intonation, speech rhythm and facial expression can change how the same words are received. Practise in pairs, exchanging guest and staff roles, and explain the situation and intended message before acting it out.

rst31-operations2-smoke-escape.title: Make smoke-avoidance actions specific
rst31-operations2-smoke-escape.text: Raise the alarm and promptly report the fire and evacuate. Choose a route away from smoke; if you must escape through smoke, keep as low as possible and cover your mouth and nose with a handkerchief or similar material to avoid inhaling smoke. Do not assume that a cloth neutralises toxic gases. Use evacuation stairs, avoid lifts, and do not return for personal belongings. Do not make finding an ordinary bag or placing it over the face a general evacuation procedure. Check routinely that exits are usable and exit signs are lit.

rst31-operations2-extinguish-principles.title: Separate extinguishing principles from conditions for action
rst31-operations2-extinguish-principles.text: Extinguishing principles include removing fuel, smothering by limiting oxygen supply and cooling by removing heat. Dilution means lowering concentration, not applying water to every fire. Some extinguishers inhibit the combustion reaction. The textbook’s nitrogen and CO2 explanation mainly concerns reduced oxygen concentration; do not treat that as identical to chemical inhibition. Choose actual equipment according to the fire types it is suitable for and the procedure in which staff have been trained. Do not pour water onto burning oil or demonstrate covering it with cloth without conditions. If you cannot maintain an escape route or fire and smoke are spreading, stop attempting to extinguish the fire and evacuate.

rst31-operations2-arson-prevention.title: Combine arson prevention with usable escape routes
rst31-operations2-arson-prevention.text: Do not accumulate combustibles in corridors, stairwells, wash areas or other blind spots; remove unnecessary items. Managers should check locks on rarely used storerooms, warehouses and empty rooms, but this does not mean blocking exits needed by people evacuating. Check entrants under store procedures and brief staff about temporary or cover workers to avoid mistaking them for intruders. Address blind spots through patrols or appropriate monitoring without invading privacy in toilets or similar places. Do not present shared customer-and-staff toilets as a universal requirement. Check the applicable noncombustibility or flame-retardancy conditions for interior materials and decorations with building management or the fire service.

rst31-operations2-training-frequency.title: Do not stop at an old “once a year” statement
rst31-operations2-training-frequency.text: The reference textbook describes annual evacuation training, but that cannot replace checking current applicability requirements. Where a building with a restaurant or other public-use premises is subject to fire management requirements, extinguishing and evacuation drills are required at least twice a year. Confirm applicability and filing or advance-notification procedures with the local fire station, then include dates in the store and building-wide fire plans. Assign reporting, extinguishing and evacuation tasks using the staff actually present on the shift, and check extinguisher suitability and use during training. Record the date, participants, problems, corrective actions and next check. Ensure both day and night shifts receive instruction by checking participation by shift and arranging catch-up training.

rst31-operations2-fire-equipment-check.title: Route six equipment checks to the appropriate people safely
rst31-operations2-fire-equipment-check.text: The textbook’s six checks concern oil on fire alarms and smoke detectors, oil on the hood fire damper, deteriorated gas hoses, the water heater’s pilot flame, automatic washer operation and pest traces in the electrical panel. The damper limits flame entry into the duct; do not leave heavy oil deposits untreated. For pilot-flame abnormalities, follow the manual and store reporting process; do not repeatedly relight equipment where gas can be smelled. Carry out the specified washer checks without bypassing safety devices to make it run. Do not touch live parts in an electrical panel; internal inspection and cleaning belong to appropriately qualified or authorised personnel. Record safe-use measures, reporting, repair arrangements and completion checks when an abnormality is found.

rst31-operations2-fire-structure-check.title: Maintain fire-protection equipment and structures
rst31-operations2-fire-structure-check.text: Have suitable personnel inspect and maintain firefighting equipment, firefighting water supplies and equipment needed for firefighting operations according to the plan. Beyond clearing escape routes, check under the building’s fire plan and checklist that fire doors, compartments and similar features can function. Do not independently wedge doors open or cover equipment during alterations. Identify who handles statutory inspections and specialist maintenance, receives results and confirms repairs. “Other necessary duties” does not mean unlimited individual discretion: define them in the plan according to the store’s use and equipment and consult the fire service.

rst31-operations2-after-evacuation.title: Separate initial actions from post-evacuation communication and prioritise life
rst31-operations2-after-evacuation.text: When calling 119, calmly answer the dispatcher’s questions: report the fire, the address firefighters should attend, the store name, landmarks and conditions. Alert people and arrange the 119 call and customer/staff evacuation in parallel as far as the available personnel allow. Only assigned people who can maintain an escape route and safety should attempt initial extinguishing or shut off heat; do not send anyone back for documents or cash. At the assembly point, report numbers, injuries and information about anyone possibly trapped to firefighters. From a safe place, contact emergency contacts, gather information from firefighters and building management, and report times, verified facts and actions taken. Re-entry and reopening require confirmation from the relevant responsible people, not an independent decision. Arrange safe document storage beforehand without delaying evacuation or prioritising retrieval. Prepare three procedures: reporting, customer evacuation and staff role allocation. Distinguish initial actions for fires, earthquakes and other disasters, and plan communication and safe guidance that the personnel present can carry out.

rst31-operations2-receipt-fine-checks.title: Detailed sorting and receiving checks
rst31-operations2-receipt-fine-checks.text: Group returns by supplier and label them with notes or box markings so everyone can identify them. Keep samples and defective goods out of usable stock, remove empty boxes and prepare measuring equipment beforehand. Use the order as the receiving baseline and check the delivery-note format, item names, unit prices, units and calculations. Check physical goods against the agreed manufacturer/origin, size, grade, pack quantity, freshness or maturation, standard usable yield, damage or temperature-change signs, and delivery date and time. Do not use out-of-specification goods; consult the responsible person and supplier. Store items in their designated ambient, chilled or frozen locations using first-in, first-out. Marking the receiving date or weekday on non-ambient goods should be combined with the store’s shelf-life controls.

rst31-operations2-qsca-and-repeat.title: Link atmosphere and hospitality to repeat visits
rst31-operations2-qsca-and-repeat.text: Q means product quality, S service, C cleanliness and A an atmosphere suited to the business format; lighting and background music also affect the guest experience. H means taking joy in another person’s happiness and applies to both customers and coworkers. Where the catchment area and spending per visit are limited, consistent experiences at appropriate prices are important for repeat visits. Remember regulars’ faces and preferred seats or dishes and express appreciation; give new customers a sound overall QSC experience that encourages them to return. Satisfied guests’ word-of-mouth or social-media recommendations may reach other new customers. Describe products accurately and respect the choice not to order extras. Off-meal-time discounts aim to attract people during quiet periods, but also check demand shifted from other times and gross profit.

rst31-operations2-staffing-service-defin.title: Align service content when using labour-hour measures
rst31-operations2-staffing-service-defin.text: Customers served per labour-hour equals customer count divided by total working hours. Full table service also requires time to take food to guests, so the same customer count may require different labour-hours. Align service content before comparing with fast-food or other formats; a higher figure is not automatically better. If training improves skills while preserving the required service level and produces the same gross profit in fewer labour-hours, gross profit per labour-hour rises. After deducting cost from sales, gross profit must still cover labour, rent, utilities and selling/administrative expenses. Do not confuse gross profit with operating profit after these expenses. A difference between rates already expressed as percentages is measured in percentage points; do not multiply the difference by 100 again.

rst31-operations2-delivery-buffer-scope.title: State the delivery period and buffer assumptions
rst31-operations2-delivery-buffer-scope.text: The textbook example orders on Monday for Tuesday delivery and on Thursday for Friday delivery. Tuesday’s receipt covers Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday demand; Friday’s covers Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Monday. It assumes stock for 120% of planned sales to allow for forecast error and explains that 110% may be sufficient with more accurate forecasting. This is not a rule to apply the same rate mechanically to every ingredient. Check lead times, shelf life, storage capacity, usable stock and confirmed incoming orders, and record the demand period separately from the basis for the buffer.

rst31-operations2-training-observation.title: Observe until independent performance is possible
rst31-operations2-training-observation.text: Learn basic service patterns by watching a demonstration and then practising repeatedly. OJT is normally one-to-one; check until the learner can perform independently to the standard, and divide long tasks into sections for practice. Observe gaze, facial expression, voice, posture and hand movements too. OFFJT is group learning away from the workplace to study principles and knowledge and link them to OJT. Distinguish voice quality, pitch and intonation from speech rhythm and emphasis at sentence endings, and ask the guest-role participant how the same guidance comes across. Check quality and safety, not speed alone.

rst31-operations2-management-purpose.title: Connect principles to work planning
rst31-operations2-management-purpose.text: Management philosophy states how the company intends to contribute to society and shares a direction for decisions about products and people. Standards specify what must be achieved in operations, while appraisal of results, ability and work behaviour identifies staffing and development needs. A training programme defines required skills, objectives and checks. A work schedule based on the sales plan assigns tasks by individual and time band, including training time. Feed planning, implementation, evaluation and corrective action into the next plan rather than merely displaying the philosophy on a wall.

rst31-operations2-figure-cost-comparison.caption: Compare standard and actual figures using the same sales base.
rst31-operations2-figure-cost-comparison.alt: Two stacked bars show standard cost at 30% and actual cost at 32%, a difference of 2 percentage points.

rst31-operations2-figure-hood-damper.caption: Check the relative positions of the hood and fire damper in a schematic section.
rst31-operations2-figure-hood-damper.alt: A schematic section shows a hood above the cooking appliance and a fire damper in the upper duct.

rst31-operations2-figure-escape-route.caption: Distinguish the route away from smoke from checks after evacuation.
rst31-operations2-figure-escape-route.alt: An independently drawn floor-plan schematic shows a route away from a smoky exit towards another opening.

rst31-operations2-q001.stem: The shift supervisor arranged cover for an absence, but the manager must approve the extra expenditure. What should happen next?
options: Hide the number of cover staff and move the expense to another category later
Approve unlimited expenditure whenever it keeps the business running
Stop even the initial safety measures because expenditure is involved
Adjust stations within the supervisor’s authority and report the cost and reasons to the manager for approval
reasons: Falsified records obstruct decisions and reporting.
Responsibility for a shift does not confer unlimited approval authority.
The involvement of expenditure does not justify stopping initial safety measures.
This combines action during the shift with the manager’s expenditure approval.
rst31-operations2-q001.explanation: This combines action during the shift with the manager’s expenditure approval.

rst31-operations2-q002.stem: In an independent exercise, dish A has a standard cost of 200 yen and sells 30 portions; dish B costs 300 yen and sells 20. What is their combined monthly standard cost?
rst31-operations2-q002.objective: Calculate standard cost from the menu mix
options: 500 yen
reasons: This is the cost of only one of the two dishes, not the total.
This adds the costs of one portion of each dish and ignores quantities sold.
Applying 300 yen to all 50 portions uses the wrong mix.

rst31-operations2-q003.stem: For the same period, an exercise gives sales of 900,000 yen, cost of 270,000 yen, a labour distribution ratio of 40% and 150 total working hours. What is labour cost per labour-hour?
rst31-operations2-q003.objective: Check the chain from gross profit to labour cost
reasons: This is gross profit divided by 150, or gross profit per labour-hour.
This applies 40% to sales and uses the wrong denominator for the labour distribution ratio.
Gross profit of 630,000 yen × 0.4 ÷ 150 = 1,680 yen.
This value does not match the formula’s cost relationships and stated conditions.

rst31-operations2-q004.stem: The textbook example orders on Monday for Tuesday delivery and on Thursday for Friday delivery. Which main sales period should Tuesday’s receipt cover before the next delivery?
rst31-operations2-q004.objective: Read the days covered by a delivery interval
options: Friday through Monday
Monday only
Tuesday only
Tuesday through Thursday
reasons: This is the period covered by Friday’s receipt.
This is before the receipt and is the wrong period.
This does not cover demand until Friday’s next receipt.
Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday demand is covered until Friday’s delivery.
rst31-operations2-q004.explanation: Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday demand is covered until Friday’s delivery.

rst31-operations2-q005.stem: Quantities, unit prices and totals on the period-end inventory sheet have been checked. What should be checked before submission under the textbook procedure?
rst31-operations2-q005.objective: Check inventory sign-off responsibilities and deadlines
options: Sign-offs by the person responsible, witness and manager, and the submission deadline
Add returns to normal stock and omit signatures
Copy last month’s signatures instead of checking this month
Choose any submission date because the calculations are correct
reasons: Correct calculations do not replace responsible sign-off and timely submission.
Both mixing returns into stock and omitting sign-off are wrong.
Last month’s confirmation cannot replace verification of this month’s facts.
Correct totals do not remove the deadline.
rst31-operations2-q005.explanation: Correct calculations do not replace responsible sign-off and timely submission.

rst31-operations2-q006.stem: You ask a guest to wait while you check their food, then return. Which pair of basic expressions is in the most appropriate order?
rst31-operations2-q006.objective: Distinguish expressions before and after a wait
options: かしこまりました (Certainly) → 失礼いたします (Excuse me)
少々お待ちください (Please wait a moment) → お待たせいたしました (Thank you for waiting)
ありがとうございました (Thank you very much) → いらっしゃいませ (Welcome)
お待たせいたしました (Thank you for waiting) → 少々お待ちください (Please wait a moment)
reasons: These acknowledge a request and introduce an action, not the two waiting stages.
This distinguishes the request to wait from the expression on returning.
These express appreciation and welcome, not the two waiting situations.
The expression used after waiting has been placed first.
rst31-operations2-q006.explanation: This distinguishes the request to wait from the expression on returning.

rst31-operations2-q007.stem: You politely introduce a request for a guest to clear the passage, then accept a different request from the guest. Which pairing of expressions and roles is correct?
rst31-operations2-q007.objective: Distinguish introducing a request from acknowledging one
options: 恐れ入りますが (Sorry to trouble you, but…) = request introduction; かしこまりました (Certainly) = acknowledgement
失礼いたします (Excuse me) = after a wait; 少々お待ちください (Please wait a moment) = apology
申し訳ございません (I am very sorry) = acknowledgement; かしこまりました (Certainly) = thanks
いらっしゃいませ (Welcome) = request introduction; ありがとうございました (Thank you) = acknowledgement
reasons: This separates a considerate request introduction from accepting the guest’s request.
The expression introducing an action and the request to wait have different meanings.
This confuses apology, acknowledgement and appreciation.
Welcome and thanks do not serve these roles.
rst31-operations2-q007.explanation: This separates a considerate request introduction from accepting the guest’s request.

rst31-operations2-q008.stem: How is a suitable person safely stopping the fuel supply classified as an extinguishing principle?
options: Removal: cutting off the combustible supply
Dilution: lowering only a liquid’s concentration
Cooling: reducing fuel temperature
Smothering: blocking only oxygen supply
reasons: Cutting off fuel uses the removal principle.
It is not dilution.
The action is not about removing heat.
The supply being stopped is fuel, not oxygen.
rst31-operations2-q008.explanation: Cutting off fuel uses the removal principle.

rst31-operations2-q009.stem: Someone proposes applying water to a kitchen oil fire because “cooling removes heat.” Which judgement is appropriate?
rst31-operations2-q009.objective: Do not generalise water use to oil fires
options: A cloth removes the need to check training and an escape route
Water is safe for every material whenever cooling is intended
Do not choose water from the principle’s name alone; do not put water on burning oil
Just increase the water without checking the oil quantity
reasons: Having a cloth does not replace training and a maintained escape route.
The extinguishing principle and the fire type it suits are separate issues.
Water on oil can cause splashing and spread the fire; check suitable equipment and training.
Changing the amount of water does not eliminate the danger.
rst31-operations2-q009.explanation: Water on oil can cause splashing and spread the fire; check suitable equipment and training.

rst31-operations2-q010.stem: What basic action should evacuees learn during smoke-escape training?
options: Choose a route with less smoke and, when needed, keep low and cover the mouth and nose while escaping
Find an ordinary bag before beginning evacuation
A lift always avoids smoke and is safe
A handkerchief completely removes toxic gases
reasons: This follows the Fire and Disaster Management Agency’s basic smoke-avoidance guidance.
Do not delay escape by prioritising a search for a bag.
Planning to use a lift during a fire is inappropriate.
Cloth does not completely remove toxic gases.
rst31-operations2-q010.explanation: This follows the Fire and Disaster Management Agency’s basic smoke-avoidance guidance.

rst31-operations2-q011.stem: Locks on an unoccupied storeroom are being checked to prevent arson. What must also be checked?
rst31-operations2-q011.objective: Combine lock control with usable escape routes
options: Leave combustibles in passages as long as the storeroom is locked
Keep necessary evacuation exits usable and distinguish controlled rooms and key responsibilities
Treat all cover staff as suspicious intruders
Lock every emergency exit from outside even while guests are present
reasons: Combustible materials must also be controlled.
This combines preventing access to empty rooms with maintaining necessary escape capability.
Briefing staff about cover workers prevents mistaken identification.
Locks that obstruct evacuation are not the intention of arson prevention.
rst31-operations2-q011.explanation: This combines preventing access to empty rooms with maintaining necessary escape capability.

rst31-operations2-q012.stem: A building containing a restaurant subject to fire management requirements plans to stop training at the old textbook’s “once a year.” What is appropriate?
rst31-operations2-q012.objective: Check old drill frequency against current applicability
options: Once annually is sufficient regardless of building use
Omit evacuation training if reporting has been practised
Confirm applicable requirements such as at least twice-yearly extinguishing/evacuation drills and advance notification with the fire station
Do not check the fire plan once a drill record exists
reasons: The old frequency alone may not meet current applicability conditions.
Reporting and evacuation are different training activities.
Plan according to the current requirements and procedures applicable to the building.
Check that the activities agree with the plan.
rst31-operations2-q012.explanation: Plan according to the current requirements and procedures applicable to the building.

rst31-operations2-q013.stem: Which function of the hood fire damper matches the textbook?
options: Bond cracks in a gas hose
Limit flame entry into the duct
Automatically weigh food
Transmit guests’ orders to the kitchen
reasons: It is not repair material or a substitute for replacing a deteriorated hose.
It helps limit fire spread, making oil-deposit checks important.
It is not a weighing instrument.
It is not an order-transmission device.
rst31-operations2-q013.explanation: It helps limit fire spread, making oil-deposit checks important.

rst31-operations2-q014.stem: A water-heater pilot-flame abnormality and pest traces in the electrical panel are reported. What should the supervisor do?
rst31-operations2-q014.objective: Identify safe responsibilities for equipment abnormalities
options: Change only the records to normal and prioritise trading
Repeatedly relight the gas before checking the cause
Secure safe use and refer matters to suitable specialists under the manual and store procedures
Have anyone dismantle the live panel to clean it
reasons: Changing records does not eliminate danger.
Independent relighting does not replace a safety check.
This connects each abnormality to suitable personnel and safety measures.
Do not casually dismantle live equipment.
rst31-operations2-q014.explanation: This connects each abnormality to suitable personnel and safety measures.

rst31-operations2-q015.stem: After evacuation, important documents are found to have been left inside. What is the appropriate next action?
options: Let one responsible person return for belongings
Report numbers and possible trapped-person information to firefighters and communicate/report from a safe place
Delay reporting until the documents have been retrieved
Reopen and prepare records before firefighters confirm safety
reasons: Do not independently permit re-entry, even by one person.
Prioritise assembly checks and information for firefighters; handle subsequent procedures safely.
Do not delay reporting to retrieve documents.
Reopening follows the relevant responsible people’s safety confirmation.
rst31-operations2-q015.explanation: Prioritise assembly checks and information for firefighters; handle subsequent procedures safely.

rst31-operations2-q016.stem: A restaurant’s serving robot reduces carrying work. Which use of the freed capacity fits QSCA and H?
rst31-operations2-q016.objective: Consider how QSCA and hospitality apply
options: Listen to customers’ and coworkers’ difficulties and respond while maintaining quality and service standards
Remove cleaning standards because carrying is automated
Press every guest to accept the same extra item without being able to refuse
Stop staff development once machinery is introduced
reasons: This combines individual consideration for guests and coworkers with maintaining standards.
Automation does not remove cleanliness standards.
This does not respect the other person’s situation and choices.
Human interaction still requires skills and development.
rst31-operations2-q016.explanation: This combines individual consideration for guests and coworkers with maintaining standards.

rst31-operations2-q017.stem: An exercise defines loss as “actual cost − standard cost.” Actual cost is 48,000 yen and standard cost 45,000 yen. Which explanation is correct?
rst31-operations2-q017.objective: Read the definition and sign of a cost loss
options: −3,000 yen; reversing subtraction keeps the same sign
+93,000 yen; add the two figures
3%; there is no difference from a yen amount
+3,000 yen; actual cost exceeds standard
reasons: Actual minus standard is positive under the stated definition.
The task calls for a difference, not a sum.
A monetary difference is in yen, and no data for converting it to a rate have been supplied.

rst31-operations2-q018.stem: Which set respectively supports repeat visits, first-time trials, customers unable to visit, and payment without cash?
options: Online delivery / cash only / points / remove telephone access
Points / website first-visit offers / online delivery / electronic payment
Same-day discounts only / notices only to regulars / in-store orders only / cash only
Electronic payment / points / only more in-store seats / cash only
reasons: The first-trial and payment-method objectives are mismatched.
All four measures match their respective objectives.
This does not serve people unable to visit or wishing to pay without cash.
Points primarily encourage return visits; cash-only payment does not meet electronic-payment preferences.
rst31-operations2-q018.explanation: All four measures match their respective objectives.

rst31-operations2-q019.stem: You recognise a guest who visits occasionally. Which response can help develop them into a regular?
options: Describe their previous private conversation in detail in front of their companion
Press them into accepting an expensive dish
Skip the greeting because they visit infrequently
Thank them for returning and offer guidance suited to their wishes
reasons: This disregards privacy and the guest’s feelings.
It does not respect the guest’s choice.
It loses an opportunity to build a relationship.
Recognition and checking preferences help build an ongoing relationship.
rst31-operations2-q019.explanation: Recognition and checking preferences help build an ongoing relationship.

rst31-operations2-q020.stem: Which approach to application documents during an interview is appropriate?
rst31-operations2-q020.objective: Determine the necessary scope of applicant information
options: Hire solely by age without considering job ability
Do not check preferred work or availability if a photograph is supplied
Avoid confusing applicants and documents, check relevant experience, and do not seek unrelated family information
Require every applicant to prove family occupations and registered domicile
reasons: This conflicts with fair selection principles.
A photograph does not replace checking job conditions.
It checks identity and relevant job information while avoiding unrelated background investigation.
Do not routinely demand information unrelated to aptitude and ability.
rst31-operations2-q020.explanation: It checks identity and relevant job information while avoiding unrelated background investigation.

rst31-operations2-q021.stem: An applicant has described their preferred role. What should the interviewer check next?
rst31-operations2-q021.objective: Compare the role, rules and applicant’s wishes
options: Stop asking because hearing requests makes hiring impossible
Confirm a job based only on the store’s convenience, regardless of preference
Hide work rules until after hiring
Compare the preferred role with store duties, explain attendance and other rules, and ask about wishes
reasons: Checking wishes helps avoid one-sided imposition of conditions.
The parties may have different understandings.
This leaves conditions and rules unclear.
Explain duties and rules while listening to wishes and matters needing discussion.
rst31-operations2-q021.explanation: Explain duties and rules while listening to wishes and matters needing discussion.

rst31-operations2-q022.stem: At a store where the relevant department must approve hiring, the interviewer wants to recruit the applicant. What should be communicated?
rst31-operations2-q022.objective: Distinguish hiring confirmation from departmental approval
options: Treat hiring as decided and make the department accept it later
Issue a confirmed offer before approval
Follow the approval process and explain how the result will be communicated
Send the applicant away without explaining how results will be communicated
reasons: This bypasses the store’s approval process.
An unapproved decision conflicts with a confirmation notice.
This combines the textbook’s approval condition with clear communication to the applicant.
The applicant would not know how to obtain the outcome.
rst31-operations2-q022.explanation: This combines the textbook’s approval condition with clear communication to the applicant.

rst31-operations2-q023.stem: Cleaning instruction states “to prevent food contamination” and “use the designated brush.” Which two elements are these?
rst31-operations2-q023.objective: Distinguish the purpose from the tools in instruction
options: Scope and time
Sequence and scope
Purpose and tools
Quality and time
reasons: They do not specify coverage or duration.
They do not describe the sequence or work boundaries.
They state why the work is done and what is used.
They do not specify the finish standard or duration.
rst31-operations2-q023.explanation: They state why the work is done and what is used.

rst31-operations2-q024.stem: Cleaning must cover the whole worktop, leave none of the specified dirt, and finish within the store’s standard time. Which interpretation is correct?
rst31-operations2-q024.objective: Distinguish scope, quality and standard time
options: All three specify tools and have nothing to do with scope
A time standard removes the need to explain quality and scope
The finish standard is scope and the work area is time
They specify scope, quality and time separately
reasons: These specify boundaries and outcomes, not equipment.
Speed alone does not define the required work.
This interchanges the elements’ meanings.
They distinguish how much, to what standard, and how long.
rst31-operations2-q024.explanation: They distinguish how much, to what standard, and how long.

rst31-operations2-q025.stem: Before teaching a task, a supervisor asks, “Who is affected if an order is misheard?” What is the main aim?
rst31-operations2-q025.objective: Understand training stages and the introductory stage
options: Permanently omit repeated practice and performance checks
Finish everyone’s assessment before learning starts
Use a familiar problem to build interest in the purpose and readiness to learn
Assign all tasks without checking ability
reasons: Demonstration, practice and assessment are still needed afterwards.
An introductory question does not replace an achievement assessment.
The introduction establishes meaning and interest.
Performance ability has not yet been checked.
rst31-operations2-q025.explanation: The introduction establishes meaning and interest.

rst31-operations2-q026.stem: With the words unchanged, staff practise pitch and intonation as well as rhythm and emphasis at sentence endings. Which elements are being checked?
options: Equipment model and quantity
Voice tone and delivery
Customer count and sales
Portion weight and usable yield
reasons: This is not an equipment check.
The practice concerns voice quality, pitch, intonation, rhythm and sentence-ending expression.
These are not the operating indicators being checked.
These are not vocal elements.
rst31-operations2-q026.explanation: The practice concerns voice quality, pitch, intonation, rhythm and sentence-ending expression.

rst31-operations2-q027.stem: Responsibilities for supervising flames, occupancy and additional equipment are unclear. What is the best way to organise them?
rst31-operations2-q027.objective: Translate fire-management duties into a specific plan
options: Skip occupancy checks during busy periods
Treat flames solely as the cooks’ issue, outside the supervisor’s awareness
Write only “other necessary duties” and leave everyone to decide independently
Consult the fire service and building management and define responsibilities and checks for the use and equipment in the fire plan
reasons: Necessary controls cannot be omitted when busy.
Supervising flame use and handling is also a fire-management duty.
A broad label alone leaves responsibility and procedures unclear.
This links general responsibilities to actual store operations.
rst31-operations2-q027.explanation: This links general responsibilities to actual store operations.

rst31-operations2-q028.stem: Cardboard has accumulated in a little-observed stairwell and behind a wash area. What arson-prevention action is appropriate?
rst31-operations2-q028.objective: Choose combustible control in blind spots
options: Move it only if it burns during evacuation
Cover it with cloth and stop checking
Ignore combustibles in passages if the storeroom is locked
Remove combustibles and include tidying and blind-spot checks in routine management
reasons: Do not leave it on the assumption that action will follow a fire.
Hiding it does not remove danger.
Locking and combustible removal are different controls.
This improves both combustible control and observation of blind spots.
rst31-operations2-q028.explanation: This improves both combustible control and observation of blind spots.

rst31-operations2-q029.stem: On a day when unfamiliar cover staff are expected, which entry-control approach is appropriate?
rst31-operations2-q029.objective: Avoid mistaking cover workers for intruders
options: Brief the responsible people on expected cover and identification methods, then check under store procedures
Classify every unfamiliar face as suspicious without asking
Do not check identity or duties for anyone described as cover staff
Make every emergency exit unusable to control entrants
reasons: Known information and procedures help prevent mistaken identification.
Legitimate cover workers may be misidentified.
Do not omit necessary entry controls.
Necessary evacuation capability must not be obstructed.
rst31-operations2-q029.explanation: Known information and procedures help prevent mistaken identification.

rst31-operations2-q030.stem: There is a blind spot near the toilets. Which monitoring plan is appropriate?
options: Define privacy-respecting patrols and appropriate monitoring areas
Treat shared customer/staff toilets as legally compulsory in every store
Stop all checks because a blind spot exists
Continuously film inside cubicles without explanation
reasons: Choose a method that meets both safety-management and privacy needs.
This turns a textbook operational example into a universal obligation.
A blind spot does not justify removing controls.
Do not adopt monitoring that invades private space.
rst31-operations2-q030.explanation: Choose a method that meets both safety-management and privacy needs.

rst31-operations2-q031.stem: A restaurant is replacing curtains. What is appropriate for fire management?
rst31-operations2-q031.objective: Check applicability of noncombustible and flame-retardant requirements
options: Guarantee that flame-retardant articles cannot burn and place them against a heat source
Check applicable flame-retardancy requirements and labels for the building and articles, and consult the responsible people on alterations
Use any preferred fabric without checking flame-retardant labels
Assume every decorative item has identical legal conditions
reasons: Flame-retardant does not mean absolutely non-burning.
Check applicability for the building use and article.
Covered articles have flame-retardancy requirements.
Distinguish conditions by article and use.
rst31-operations2-q031.explanation: Check applicability for the building use and article.

rst31-operations2-q032.stem: Oil is found on a detector and an automatic washer operates abnormally. What is appropriate?
rst31-operations2-q032.objective: Link detector and washer checks to suitable corrective action
options: Report abnormalities under safe procedures and assign suitable cleaning/inspection and completion checks
Stop checking the dirty detector if the washer runs
Hide the detector’s appearance and change only the record to normal
Bypass the safety device to make the washer run
reasons: This turns detected abnormalities into reporting and correction.
Abnormalities in different devices do not cancel one another.
Hiding the appearance or changing records leaves the danger.
Bypassing a safety device does not establish normal operation.
rst31-operations2-q032.explanation: This turns detected abnormalities into reporting and correction.

rst31-service1-a001.title: Check expectations, value and comfort separately
rst31-service1-a001.text: Customer expectations arise from experience, knowledge, atmosphere and price. Review experience against expectations: better means satisfaction, similar means ordinary, lower means dissatisfaction; value for money also matters. Assess freshness/appearance as well as flavour, and facilities/appearance as well as staff attitude. If food is ready but room temperature, lighting or time-inappropriate music prevents relaxation, improve atmosphere and comfort.

rst31-service1-a002.title: Initiate greetings
rst31-service1-a002.text: When noticing guests at the entrance, greet first in a way suited to them. Do not vary service solely with your mood; communicate welcome with a gentle gaze and audible voice. This does not universally require shouting or prolonged staring. Practise acknowledging guests and involving the seating staff even when your hands are occupied.

rst31-service1-a003.title: Match honoured/lower seats to layout and preferences
rst31-service1-a003.text: Learn the honoured seat as the comfortable, safe side in context and the lower seat as a position used, for example, by hosts. In Japanese rooms, the alcove and entrance provide clues. Do not infer rank from appearance and force seats. Check preferences with the booking representative and consider access and serving routes before seating.

rst31-service1-a004.title: Distinguish Western dining examples from clearing
rst31-service1-a004.text: The source’s dining example starts food from the left except some desserts and gathers leftovers at the front of the plate. This teaches dining conventions, not grounds for rushing guests. Observe meal progress, utensils and napkins and ask whether the guest is still eating before clearing.

rst31-service1-a005.title: Check wheelchair type and seating conditions
rst31-service1-a005.text: Attendant-propelled wheelchairs are mainly operated by helpers; self-propelled ones by users turning the wheels. Type alone does not determine assistance needs. Check steps, routes and preferences before considering safe store support. If table height/legroom fit, offer a place usable without transferring. Do not move or transfer someone without their agreement.

rst31-service1-a006.title: Check assistance-dog markings/documents politely
rst31-service1-a006.text: White/yellow harnesses help identify guide dogs; service/hearing dogs carry type markings and other information. MHLW guidance says users carry certification and health-management records. When verification is needed, explain why and politely check certification with the user. Do not summon the dog to test it or move the dog away from its user.

rst31-service1-a007.title: Connect six marks to support
rst31-service1-a007.text: The assistance-dog mark promotes understanding of the Assistance Dogs Act; the ear mark prompts consideration of hearing difficulty. The ostomate mark concerns people with bowel/urinary stomas and suitable facilities; Heart Plus concerns less-visible internal physical disabilities. Help Mark signals assistance/consideration needs not apparent externally; the maternity mark prompts support for pregnant/postpartum people. Do not infer diagnoses; ask about writing, facility guidance, rest seating or other needed support.

rst31-service1-a008.title: Read takeaway numbers as conditional examples
rst31-service1-a008.text: The source gives 10℃ or below as a cooling-control example, not identical temperatures/deadlines for every dish. Check dish, elapsed time after cooking, container and storage with the manager, then communicate store-set temperature controls and consumption deadlines. If storage advice is unknown, verify it rather than borrowing numbers from another product.

rst31-service1-a009.title: Check the roles of polite expressions
rst31-service1-a009.text: “失礼いたします” (excuse me) may be said both when approaching and leaving a table. “存じ上げております” politely states knowledge; “そうさせていただきます” states an action based on permission and related circumstances. Do not mechanically add polite-sounding words: check facts and permission. Source forms include “奥様” (madam/wife), “旦那様” (sir/husband) and “お使いの方” (a person sent on an errand), but respect known names and preferred forms of address.

rst31-service1-a010.title: Show telephone listening through speech
rst31-service1-a010.text: Callers cannot see nods or facial expressions. Use spoken acknowledgements and ask again where unclear. Before questions use “恐れ入りますが” (sorry to trouble you, but…); before transfers explain the connection and waiting. Repeat and record contact numbers rather than passing on assumed hearing.

rst31-service1-a011.title: Check allergen-labelling date and scope
rst31-service1-a011.text: Distinguish packaged processed-food labelling from restaurant information. The Consumer Affairs Agency’s 1 April 2026 amendment added cashews to specified ingredients. The nine are shrimp, crab, walnuts, wheat, buckwheat, eggs, milk, peanuts and cashews. Cashews have transition arrangements until 31 March 2028, so absence from a label does not prove non-use. Do not answer from an old eight-item list; confirm current supplier information and cooking processes with the manager.

rst31-service1-a012.title: Combine nutrients across the meal
rst31-service1-a012.text: Do not judge meals by protein alone, vegetables alone or another single element. Learn balanced daily combinations of the five major nutrients. Identify foods in staple, main and side dishes and recognise that one ingredient contains multiple nutrients. Staff must not guess individual treatment or guaranteed nutrient quantities.

rst31-service1-a013.title: Use detergents/soaking under specified conditions
rst31-service1-a013.text: Even with strong detergents, check purpose, warnings, protection and procedures. Do not improvise mixing or stronger concentrations; protect food/guests. Soaking with detergent in about 40℃ water is an example for loosening adhered soil, not a specified temperature for every vessel/chemical. Prioritise actual material/product conditions.

rst31-service1-a014.title: Separate confirmed facts from unresolved complaint decisions
rst31-service1-a014.text: After listening, promptly apologise/report when your or the store’s mistake is confirmed. If unable to judge causes/responses, say “責任者を呼んでまいります” (I will get the person responsible) and hand over. The manager checks and decides, with staff present where needed. If feelings remain unsettled, consider changing person/place/timing; do not promise refunds without authority.

rst31-service1-a015.title: Go beyond removing an insect
rst31-service1-a015.text: If an insect appears in guest areas, act promptly under store methods without spreading it to food/guests and report place/time. Investigate sources/entry such as open doors, waste and equipment gaps. Captured counts alone do not finish the task; improve cleaning and exclusion. Do not independently spray chemicals near food.

rst31-service1-a016.title: Divide illness care and vomit-cleanup roles
rst31-service1-a016.text: Check breathing/consciousness, seek help and monitor an unwell person. Offer a rest area only after assessing condition/safety; do not advise water universally. Vomit may be infectious: prevent people walking through it, and have designated staff work quietly with disposable gloves, masks/aprons. Use dedicated tools/store disinfection procedures through disposal and handwashing. Do not teach improvised chemical concentrations.

rst31-service1-a017.title: Do not postpone calls in choking
rst31-service1-a017.text: FDMA guidance encourages continued coughing while effective and close observation. If choking is suspected, such as inability to speak or weak coughing, immediately request 119/emergency help rather than waiting for removal. Report loss of responsiveness and follow dispatcher/trained lifesaving steps. Infant techniques differ from others; this text does not replace formal practical training.

rst31-service1-a018.title: Choose actions for shaking, fire and smoke conditions
rst31-service1-a018.text: During strong shaking protect yourself where falling/toppling/moving objects pose less risk, such as under a sturdy table. Guide guests after shaking stops and surroundings/routes are checked. If fire reaches the ceiling or smoke obscures vision, prioritise evacuation rather than continuing initial firefighting. Guide along safe routes in a low posture to limit smoke inhalation; do not delay to find towels. Tell people not to return for belongings.

rst31-service1-a019.title: Identify banknotes/coins through official specimens
rst31-service1-a019.text: Check denomination figures and designs together. Notes first issued in 2024 show: 10,000 yen Shibusawa Eiichi/Tokyo Station; 5,000 yen Tsuda Umeko/wisteria; 1,000 yen Kitasato Shibasaburo/The Great Wave off Kanagawa from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Distinguish older Fukuzawa Yukichi, Higuchi Ichiyo and Noguchi Hideyo notes and the 2,000-yen note, with Shureimon on the front and Tale of Genji imagery on the back. New issuance alone does not invalidate older notes. Read 1, 5, 10, 50, 100 and 500 yen coins; compare official front/back images to see holes in 5/50 yen coins. The 500 yen also has old/new designs, so colour alone does not decide value/validity. Read back received amounts and use equipment/store checks. These Ministry of Finance specimens are not authentication training.

rst31-service1-a020.title: Distinguish choking techniques and responsiveness transitions
rst31-service1-a020.text: When choking is suspected, request 119/help without waiting for treatment to finish. In a responsive adult, distinguish back blows first from abdominal thrusts if ineffective. Back blows use the heel of the hand between the shoulder blades. Do not universally apply abdominal thrusts to infants, pregnant people or severely obese people. Infants require different methods: check current official materials and appropriate training. If unresponsive, call 119 if not already done and move to CPR procedures. Distinguish unresponsiveness with normal breathing: side-lying recovery position and monitoring. Use official videos for theory and practical courses for posture/force; diagrams alone do not certify skill.

rst31-service1-term-genever.title: Genever
rst31-service1-term-genever.text: A name given in the textbook as an example of a gin type. Check the served product’s type and ingredients against the menu and labelling.

rst31-service1-link-assistance.title: Check the assistance-dog mark on the official page
rst31-service1-link-assistance.text: Check the official form and explanation of the assistance-dog mark on the rights holder’s or public authority’s page.

rst31-service1-link-ear.title: Check the ear mark on the official page
rst31-service1-link-ear.text: Check the official form and explanation of the ear mark on the rights holder’s or public authority’s page.

rst31-service1-link-ostomate.title: Check the ostomate symbol on the official page
rst31-service1-link-ostomate.text: Check the official form and explanation of the ostomate symbol on the rights holder’s or public authority’s page.

rst31-service1-link-heart.title: Check the Heart Plus mark on the official page
rst31-service1-link-heart.text: Check the official form and explanation of the Heart Plus mark on the rights holder’s or public authority’s page.

rst31-service1-link-help.title: Check the Help Mark on the official page
rst31-service1-link-help.text: Check the official form and explanation of the Help Mark on the rights holder’s or public authority’s page.

rst31-service1-link-maternity.title: Check the maternity mark on the official page
rst31-service1-link-maternity.text: Check the official form and explanation of the maternity mark on the rights holder’s or public authority’s page.

rst31-service1-link-choking-conscious.title: Official airway-obstruction material for a responsive person
rst31-service1-link-choking-conscious.text: Check intended persons, posture and procedures in official FDMA video material. Practise practical skills in lifesaving training.

rst31-service1-link-choking-unresponsive.title: Official airway-obstruction material for an unresponsive person
rst31-service1-link-choking-unresponsive.text: Check intended persons, posture and procedures in official FDMA video material. Practise practical skills in lifesaving training.

rst31-service1-link-recovery.title: Official recovery-position material
rst31-service1-link-recovery.text: Check intended persons, posture and procedures in official FDMA video material. Practise practical skills in lifesaving training.

rst31-service1-link-infant-current.title: Check infant methods in current official material
rst31-service1-link-infant-current.text: Infant methods differ from adults. Check the Children and Families Agency’s current JRC2025-based illustrations and links to official videos.

rst31-service1-fig001.caption: Compare slight bows about 15°, formal bows about 30° and deepest bows about 45°. Keep the back straight rather than bending only the neck.
rst31-service1-fig001.alt: Three bows in side view, comparing straight torso inclinations pivoting at the hips.

rst31-service1-fig002.caption: The non-dominant hand supports the tray centre. Check the example of loading heavy items from the body side and unloading from the finger side.
rst31-service1-fig002.alt: Top-view transparent tray showing palm/spread fingers, heavy plate near the body and small plate near fingertips.

rst31-service1-fig003.caption: Support the lower glass and underside of plates; avoid touching drinking rims or food.
rst31-service1-fig003.alt: Two diagrams of a hand holding a glass’s lower half and a hand supporting plate rim/underside.

rst31-service1-fig004.caption: Compare spread inverted-V-shaped cutlery with aligned diagonal cutlery. Check meal progress and wishes before clearing.
rst31-service1-fig004.alt: Two plates showing inverted-V-spread and diagonally aligned utensils.

rst31-service1-fig005.caption: An example of Japanese-room/round-table seating. Use entrance/alcove clues while checking preferences and mobility.

rst31-service1-q001.stem: A guest says the experience matched prior expectations. Which textbook comparison fits best?
options: Highest satisfaction regardless of price
Ordinary, matching expectations
Dissatisfaction below expectations
Delight far above expectations
reasons: This ignores the price/value relationship.
This fits experience matching expectations.
Experience did not fall below expectations.
There is no evidence of far exceeding them.
rst31-service1-q001.explanation: Distinguish above, equal to and below expectations. Equal fits the ordinary comparison.

rst31-service1-q002.stem: A first-time guest says, “At this price and with this frontage, I expected a relaxing meal.” What does this show?
options: Price and store impressions influence expectations
Expectations cannot arise before eating
Only staff tenure determines expectations
Everyone has identical expectations at the same price
reasons: The guest describes a level anticipated from price/atmosphere.
Anticipated standards exist before use.
Guest experience/knowledge also matter.
Prior experience/knowledge differ between people.
rst31-service1-q002.explanation: Read the anticipated standard in the guest’s words; multiple factors affect expectations.

rst31-service1-q003.stem: Which pairing fits physical and service aspects of atmosphere?
options: Both mean food prices only
Physical means staff attitude; service means entrance equipment
Physical means booking calls; service means seating lights
Physical means store appearance; service means staff attitude
reasons: Price alone does not explain atmosphere.
Attitude/equipment are reversed.
Telephone service/lighting are reversed.
Appearance is physical; attitude is interpersonal.
rst31-service1-q003.explanation: Separating appearance/equipment from food/service/attitude makes improvement areas concrete.

rst31-service1-q004.objective: Check eyes and mouth in smiling
rst31-service1-q004.stem: Which fits the textbook’s three aspects of a service smile?
options: Loud speech makes facial checks unnecessary
Combine eyes, mouth and consideration for the other person
Open eyes wide and stare continuously
Move only mouth corners, ignoring the guest
reasons: Volume does not replace facial expression.
This combines gentle gaze, mouth and consideration.
The source does not recommend continuous staring.
Mouth movement alone does not check conveyed gaze/feeling.
rst31-service1-q004.explanation: Practise gentle eyes/mouth with colleagues checking how it is received.

rst31-service1-q005.stem: Practising a formal bow with a straight back, where is the source’s gaze guideline?
options: Above the guest’s head
About 2 m ahead of the feet
At your own feet
About 1 m ahead of the feet
reasons: This is not the above-head example.
About 2 m is the slight-bow example.
The feet are the deepest-bow example.
About 1 m is the formal-bow example.
rst31-service1-q005.explanation: Distinguish gaze examples as well as angles for slight/formal/deep bows; check posture/store practice in actual service.

rst31-service1-q006.stem: Which combines the source’s stable loading example and unloading order?
options: Load heavy items from the body side; unload from the finger side
Cluster tall items near fingers and unload from one side only
Load outer edges regardless of weight and unload nearest first
Load heavy items near fingers first; unload body side first
reasons: This matches heavy items in the stable near-body position and unloading from fingers.
Do not put tall items on the unstable finger side.
Edge concentration destabilises the centre of gravity.
Both heavy-item position and unloading side reverse the example.
rst31-service1-q006.explanation: Check body/finger sides relative to the supporting hand and changing centre of gravity.

rst31-service1-q007.stem: Which basic tray support matches the source?
options: Support the centre with the opposite palm, fingers spread
Pinch only the rim with the dominant hand, elbow fully extended
Close fingers at one point and extend towards guests
Put it on the shoulder to free both hands
reasons: This matches palm-centre support, spread fingers and a right-angle elbow.
Rim-only support differs from centre support.
Point support/projecting towards guests undermines stability.
It is not a shoulder-carrying method.
rst31-service1-q007.explanation: Check support position, spread fingers and elbow shape together.

rst31-service1-q008.stem: Which matches the right-handed chopstick example?
options: Hold upper steady, move only lower
Hold lower steady, move upper
Keep crossed and move both together
Grip vertically and stab with tips
reasons: This reverses the moving chopstick.
This matches upper/lower roles.
The example is not crossed sticks.
The source does not show a stabbing grip.
rst31-service1-q008.explanation: Learn to stabilise the lower and move the upper rather than both.

rst31-service1-q009.objective: Understand the alcove as a seating clue
options: Always immediately beside every room entrance
The seat itself, always overriding guest wishes
A display space for hanging scrolls etc., giving a seating clue
A clearing route outside the entrance
reasons: Many examples are far from the entrance, not universally beside it.
It names a space, not a rule overriding wishes.
This matches the display-space/seating-clue relationship.
It is not a clearing route.
rst31-service1-q009.explanation: Even with the alcove located, check preferences/mobility when allocating seats.

options: Inverted V means finished; diagonal alignment means eating
Inverted V means eating; diagonal alignment means finished
Both signal extra orders
Both refuse utensil replacement
reasons: The example meanings are reversed.
This matches the two examples.
They are not shown as extra-order signals.
They do not mean refusing replacements.
rst31-service1-q010.explanation: Utensil position is a clue; check with the guest before clearing.

options: Fold away; cover food when leaving
Fold always right; throw on chair after finishing
Fold towards you; loosely fold at table left when finished
Always put on floor when leaving or finished
reasons: Fold/leaving treatment differ from the example.
Direction/rough placement are inappropriate.
This matches fold and finished position.
The example does not use the floor.
rst31-service1-q011.explanation: Distinguish chair placement during absence from table-left placement after finishing; confirm meal progress.

rst31-service1-q012.objective: Do not decide support from wheelchair type alone
rst31-service1-q012.stem: Which is appropriate for attendant/self-propelled chairs?
options: Self-propelled users never need help even at steps
Type alone decides transfer suitability
Attendant chairs are mainly operated by helpers, but ask the user what is needed
Staff must push attendant chairs without consulting users
reasons: Self-propelled users may need help depending on the environment.
Type alone cannot decide transfers.
This separates type features from checking with the user.
Do not operate without agreement.
rst31-service1-q012.explanation: Type is an observation clue; check wishes, steps, routes and safe methods.

rst31-service1-q013.objective: Choose seating usable in a wheelchair
rst31-service1-q013.stem: A guest wants to remain in the wheelchair. What should be checked?
options: Only whether accompanied
Only wheelchair/interior colour match
Only whether transfer can be required
Suitable table height and legroom
reasons: Companionship alone does not decide.
Colour is not a usability condition.
Do not force transfer against wishes.
This checks usable space.
rst31-service1-q013.explanation: Check routes/table conditions and guide to usable seating.

rst31-service1-q014.stem: Verification of an assistance dog is needed. What is appropriate?
options: Command the dog to test obedience
Separate it into another room
Politely ask the user to show certification
Ignore markings and refuse all as pets
reasons: Staff must not disrupt work to test the dog.
Do not separate user/dog without permission.
This follows MHLW guidance.
Do not universally refuse assistance dogs.
rst31-service1-q014.explanation: Check markings/necessary documents with the user and avoid attracting the dog’s attention.

rst31-service1-q015.stem: Which mark concerns people with bowel/urinary stomas and suitable toilets?
options: Assistance-dog mark
Ear mark
Ostomate mark
Maternity mark
reasons: It promotes understanding of the Assistance Dogs Act.
It concerns consideration for hearing difficulty.
It concerns ostomates and suitable facilities.
It concerns pregnant/postpartum people.
rst31-service1-q015.explanation: Go beyond names: connect meanings to support such as facility guidance.

options: Only deaf people
Only pregnant people
Certifies assistance-dog type
Internal physical disabilities not easily visible
reasons: This confuses the ear mark.
This confuses the maternity mark.
It does not replace assistance-dog markings/documents.
It promotes understanding of internal disabilities.
rst31-service1-q016.explanation: Do not infer health from appearance; ask about needed consideration.

rst31-service1-q017.stem: Which understanding of a Help Mark user is appropriate?
options: No visible difficulty means no consideration needed
Assistance/consideration needs may not be outwardly apparent
It only locates disabled facilities
All wearers have the same disease
reasons: Do not deny needs from appearance.
This matches signalling less-visible needs.
It is not only a facility-location mark.
It does not indicate one specific disease.
rst31-service1-q017.explanation: Do not standardise support; ask wishes if the person appears to need help.

rst31-service1-q018.stem: Which is appropriate for cashew labelling amended in April 2026?
options: Added to specified ingredients, but labels alone do not prove non-use during transition
All restaurant dishes acquired exactly packaged-food labelling duties
The old eight-item list completes ingredient checks
Missing labelling removes shared-tool checks
reasons: This considers both addition and transition.
This confuses packaged-food rules with restaurant information.
Old materials alone can miss amendments/ingredient changes.
Labelling alone does not rule out contamination.
rst31-service1-q018.explanation: Check date/scope and enquire into current purchasing information/processes.

rst31-service1-q019.objective: Check differences from the old list
rst31-service1-q019.stem: Which ingredient was added to specified ingredients on 1 April 2026?
options: Sesame
Soybean
Cashew nuts
Almonds
reasons: Not the addition in this amendment.
Not the addition in this amendment.
This moved into specified ingredients in this amendment.
Not the addition in this amendment.
rst31-service1-q019.explanation: Check the nine-item list adding cashews to the old eight, including transition arrangements.

rst31-service1-q020.stem: Which example/category pairing matches the source?
options: Cider—brandy
Cognac—gin
Genever—gin
London gin—sake
reasons: Cider exemplifies fermented apple fruit wine.
Cognac exemplifies brandy.
Genever is a gin-name example.
London gin is a gin-name example.
rst31-service1-q020.explanation: Connect names/categories and check individual product labels.

rst31-service1-q021.objective: Distinguish soaking examples from specified conditions
rst31-service1-q021.stem: How should the textbook’s soaking example at about 40℃ be used?
options: Require about 40℃ for every detergent/vessel
Mix detergents for the same effect
Higher temperature removes the need to read warnings
Learn soil-loosening purpose and check material/product specifications
reasons: Do not generalise one example to all products.
Do not improvise mixing.
Temperature does not replace warning labels.
This separates purpose from actual specified conditions.
rst31-service1-q021.explanation: Soaking loosens soil; actual work checks materials, detergent, protection and store procedures.

rst31-service1-q023.stem: A guest vomits in the seating area. Which prevents spread?
options: Keep rubbing widely with normal table cloths
Let guests walk through until dry
Skip protection if the guest drank alcohol
Keep people away and clean quietly with dedicated protection/tools
reasons: This can spread contamination elsewhere.
Prevent spread through footsteps/drying.
Do not omit protection based on guessed causes.
Control access/tools to prevent spread.
rst31-service1-q023.explanation: Inform the manager; designated staff follow store disinfection/disposal and subsequent handwashing.

rst31-service1-q024.objective: Do not delay choking emergency calls
rst31-service1-q024.stem: An eating guest cannot speak and coughs weakly. When should help be requested?
options: Immediately request 119/help when choking is suspected
Only after consciousness is lost
Wait until repeated attempts fail
After closing and recording
reasons: Secure help/calling at suspicion.
Do not wait for unconsciousness.
Do not make calling depend on treatment success.
This cannot wait for a business break.
rst31-service1-q024.explanation: Current FDMA guidance requests immediate 119 calling once choking is identified.

rst31-service1-q025.objective: Choose a response to effective coughing
rst31-service1-q025.stem: Food seems lodged but coughing is effective. What is basic care?
options: Encourage continued coughing and monitor closely
Stop coughing and make them gulp water
Insert fingers deeply without knowing techniques
Leave alone until recovery
reasons: With effective coughing, encourage it and watch changes.
This obstructs coughing clearance and adds drinking risks.
Do not improvise searching for unseen foreign bodies.
Do not miss weakening cough or other changes.
rst31-service1-q025.explanation: Weak coughing/inability to speak requires immediate calling/help.

rst31-service1-q026.stem: Strong shaking continues. Which is a basic falling-object shelter?
options: Immediately in front of glass
Under a sturdy table or space without dangerous falling items
Near hot-pot worktables
Beside tall stacked dish cupboards
reasons: Glass may break/fall.
Choose protection from falling/toppling/moving hazards.
Hot objects may spill.
Shelves/items may fall/topple.
rst31-service1-q026.explanation: Secure yourself first; after shaking stops check surroundings/escape routes.

rst31-service1-q027.objective: Understand when to stop initial firefighting
rst31-service1-q027.stem: Flames reach the ceiling and smoke obscures vision. What now?
options: Approach the fire for tools
Stop continued firefighting and prioritise evacuation
Ask guests to take over
Always continue until the extinguisher is empty
reasons: Do not increase danger by approaching.
Prioritise evacuation when initial firefighting becomes difficult.
Do not assign dangerous firefighting to guests.
Do not prioritise exhausting contents as danger grows.
rst31-service1-q027.explanation: Ceiling spread/poor visibility do not justify continuing. Evacuate by a safe route and do not return.

rst31-service1-q028.stem: Which basic posture fits guidance to a safe route through smoke?
options: Keep the face high to inspect smoke
Make everyone wait until towels are found
Promise lifts always avoid smoke
Evacuate as low as possible
reasons: Do not bring the face near smoke accumulating above.
Do not delay evacuation to find items.
Do not universally direct people to lifts in fires.
This reduces smoke inhalation.
rst31-service1-q028.explanation: Use a low posture on a safe route; do not delay for belongings or return afterwards.

rst31-service1-q029.objective: Do not generalise adult techniques to everyone
rst31-service1-q029.stem: Which understanding of choking first aid is correct?
options: Methods depend on person/responsiveness; confirm separate infant methods
Use adult abdominal thrusts identically on infants
Keep unresponsive people standing and continue unchanged
Use abdominal thrusts on pregnant people regardless of body condition
reasons: Check methods by person/responsiveness.
Infant methods differ; do not generalise adults’ techniques.
Loss of responsiveness requires switching to CPR procedures.
Pregnancy is an abdominal-thrust exclusion.
rst31-service1-q029.explanation: Do not delay 119. Use official person/responsiveness-specific procedures; theory diagrams do not certify practical skill.
